utterances.text: Mr. Hogic, you see where there is reference to Atif Krdzic, the commander of the military police on the 22nd of November 1992, a little further down in that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HOGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute. Yes. The staff appointed Atif Krdzic the commander of the Srebrenica OS military police on the 22nd of November 1992. That's what it says in the document, which means that as of that time he probably held that position.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, I'd ask you just to turn back to the beginning of the document and noting the date the 19th of September 1993. Was that prior to or was that after the demilitarisation of the Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't we know it all? He's not the only witness who has come here to tell us what the demilitarisation took place. We all know when it took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly Your Honour, but this leads to the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you agree that this document tends to indicate that the military police was still in formation or existed after the demilitarisation date?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HOGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Hogic, also you've testified that it's difficult for a police, military police force that didn't have many resources to function. And would you agree with me that they might not be able to function to their top ability or they could only function or not function?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's a completely again it's a leading question. The formula, "Will you agree with me," and then a proposition is put and a proposition which isn't open. It's a very specific suggestion to the witness. The witness is only going to answer yes. It only invites a yes answer. I would request my learned friend to rephrase in a non-leading way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think you need to rephrase the question because as it is, you even asked the witness to suppose, to make suppositions too. But anyway, please rephrase the question, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Hogic, if a police unit did not have all the means, would its choices be either completely -- it could be completely non-functional or that it would function at different levels or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HOGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a unit in such a situation within the context of demilitarisation could have functioned very inefficiently. If a unit has no weapons, if it couldn't move around the zone where there were UNPROFOR units, well, then how could it have functioned? I think its functioning had been reduced to a minimum, and it's difficult to believe that the way in which it functioned was effective. It functioned more on paper than in reality.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And in terms of predemilitarisation, could it function more effectively then?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HOGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's an assumption, naturally. It could have if it had been armed. If it had all the resources that such a unit required, then it certainly could have functioned in a more effective manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'd like to show Mr. Hogic Prosecution Exhibit 458, please. In the English version, while I would like him to glance through the entire document, it's quite lengthy, but in the English version I'm looking particularly at pages 25 through 30 on up to 33, and the ERN numbers in the B/C/S version would be 03593159 to 03593172.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you just take a minute, please, to glance through those pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The English version, pages 30 to 33.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, I believe it's 25, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 25 to 30 on up to 33.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 25 we start from.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It's in Sanction also. We are on page 25 in Sanction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm really trying to understand what is going on here, naturally we don't have all the Prosecutor's documents at hand and I can't understand what sort of a document this is. Could the Prosecutor inform us of the nature of this document. It probably has a title and I would like to know whether this is a document the authenticity of which we have put into question. Please could you inform us of the nature of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Having mentioned the document number, isn't that enough? We are talking of Prosecution Exhibit 458. If you don't have it available, we can make it available. There is no question about it. But --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's not on the list. We don't have it at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in re-examination. What I'm saying is that if you need it to be made available, we can put it on the Sanction, on the -- we can actually divide the page on the monitor, if it is at all possible, or else we can put the B/C/S version on the ELMO and you can watch it from there. And the witness can watch it from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it would be of assistance now and in the future if we could always be informed of the title of the document so that we can know which document is in question. That's all I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sometimes even mentioning the title of the document is not the correct way of proceeding, Ms. Vidovic, and I think I don't need to explain why.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour I can certainly mention the title of the document if that would assist our learned friends. This document is "Military Police Records from Srebrenica." We refer to it commonly as the military log. I believe that Defence counsel has seen the original version and were using what is already previously been entered in as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any way, let's move as fast as we can. Let's put the B/C/S version on the ELMO and the witness can follow from there and Madam Vidovic can follow from there. We start from page 25 or sorry, on we start from -- I now miss the -- the ERN number of the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: ERN number of the first page -- I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Hogic, when you glance through this document, could you please comment on the level of functionability that you see illustrated or not illustrated in the document.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HOGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I have just had a look at consists of records made by someone. It looks like a sort of notebook rather than an official document. It looks like the notebook of someone who performed security duties. I'm not familiar with the signature that I can see here. I don't know who this person is. I can see that Nazif Krdzic is mentioned on the first page. And the date the 26th of December 1992 is referred to. But I can't read it very clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move with the pages, please. Let's see the next one. And no comments on your part, Witness, please. We'll just ask the question at the end.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next page, please. Next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But Your Honour, it's impossible for me to read this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I believe the witness is supposed to be looking at the B/C/S on the ELMO, Your Honour, and I believe he might be looking in Sanction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Look -- I don't know what mode -- he's looking at the ELMO, yeah. Yes, I mean take them in your hand and we can follow on the -- on Sanction. And you don't need to go through the details, just skim through what you have there because the question is a very simple one, what does that document or the parts of that document that you are reading tell you about the functionability of the unit at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And obviously Your Honour, if anything and if what it states is true. This is one of the documents that we have not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That wasn't put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But it obviously it shouldn't be suggested to him that this is a genuine article in any sense and that he should take --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But it cannot be suggested -- the opposite or the contrary cannot be suggested to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. It has to be open.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question is a very simple one. What it shows on the face of it, that document, what does it tell you about the functionability. There was, as I understood it, the question that Ms. Sellers was asking.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour that is exactly the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What if anything does it tell him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not an official document. It's a record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Assuming that what you see there is what the document contains, that's what the document says. It's none of your business whether that is correct or not correct, whether the information is full, false, entire, or whatever. The only question is this: Looking at what you have there, what does that tell you about the functionability of the unit at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I can see from this document is that one member of the military police recorded the way in which that unit functioned. It tells me nothing else. I hope that I've been clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So basically what is being put to you by the Prosecution is, does that tell you that, indeed, the military police were functioning? This is basically the question. Now, whether it's true or not, that is another matter. That will be seen by us. But according to what you see in that document, would that mean that the military police was functioning or were functioning or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was probably functioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would go now to my last --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please because --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I go now to the last question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since the Prosecutor has introduced a number of new documents, and this did not relate to the questions that we put, I would have a few brief questions that I would like to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ask your colleague whether that is regular or not. Let's finish, Ms. Sellers, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Then the last couple of questions, Mr. Hogic you indicated, testified in your cross-examination that when the military police is under two bodies, it might be difficult to have a clear command structure. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HOGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like to read out something from tape number 17. I understand that we have handouts that we can provide for expediency's sake. This is tape 2920, videotape 2920 of the interview. It's on page 20 in the English version that I will be reading. Tape 17. It's P329.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What page, Ms. Sellers, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It is page -- I have page 19. It is the videotape 9. I understand we are going to go from 19 to 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Indicated to me it's page 20. I will read: "Question: Was it military police that were in charge of the prison? "Answer: N-O. Of course this was the duty of the head of the military police and what the military police were doing there. This was also the duty of Hamid Salihovic who was carrying out the interrogation of these prisoners. I had much bigger problems elsewhere, protecting villages from Chetnik attacks and from Chetnik breakthroughs. "Question: There is no question that those are big problems. Is the military police a branch of the military under which -- of which you were the commander? "Answer: Yes." Now, does that indicate, Mr. Hogic, a clearer chain of command and subordination?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yet again it's being put in a leading way. What my learned friend should ask is what if anything does it indicate about the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you are right, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase and we can use Mr. Jones' question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: What if anything does that indicate about the chain of command, what has just been read out to you, Mr. Hogic?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HOGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It does indicate something about the chain of command. It indicates something about the relation between the superior, between a superior and his subordinate.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Does it indicate that the military police were subordinated to the commander?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HOGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It would have had to be subordinated to the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Hogic. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just say one thing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes are we going to give this a number or shall I -- I think we will need to -- we already have two from these, the previous ones that I gave you. Yes, Mr. Jones in the meantime -- all right. I mean we need to give it a number? We can compile together with the others and give them a number but the Defence must know what the reference number is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour we will provide the Bench and Defence with complete copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Simply to sigh this, Your Honour: That Your Honour referred my colleague to me on the issue of questions after re-examination and I told her that of course if new matters come up in re-examination, we are allowed to ask questions, otherwise it would be a denial of our right to cross-examine and I'm sure that's what Your Honour has in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But there are no new things that have ace arisen, Mr. Jones, and that's quite clear. What has arisen are questions that you would have put yourself on cross-examination. Do you have any questions, Judge Brydensholt? Do you have any questions, Judge Eser?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I'm still in need of clarification with regard to this issue of having knowledge of certain decrees, laws and so on. I would like to demonstrate my question with regard to an exhibit which has been produced both by the Prosecution and by the Defence. That is P54 [sic]. I don't need -- I think that we need it on the ELMO. It's dealing with reports that have been disciplinary measures taken, pronounced in certain months. And this document, at the end, they would complain and request again to send collections of legal regulations. Now, my question is: At the same time or before that request, they had pronounced quite a few measures, disciplinary measures, like reprimands, warnings, military detention. Now, how do I have to understand this? Did these measures, have these measures been taken without having any legal material at hand? Or was it possible to decide because there was still some sort of material available to base decisions, sanctions, and things like this on?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I note the witness answered the first question yes. It wasn't interpreted. He actually nodded and said DA when Your Honour said did these measures, have these measures been taken without any legal material at hand. The witness responded. For some reason it wasn't picked up.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I did not hear him. But he's here and he can confirm it any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: My question was had this decision been taken without having any material or what else has been the basis of taking these decisions?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HOGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you remember, I said that this was probably done without there being a real, legal basis, but it was probably on the basis of certain experience that lawyers in Srebrenica had at the time or they perhaps improvised at the time. If you have a look at the kind of punishment meted out to the soldiers, you will see that it's different from the sort of punishment provided for by the provisions on discipline within the ABiH at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. I thank you, Judge Eser. Mr. Hogic, we've come to the end of your testimony. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, I would like to thank you very much for having come here to give evidence in this case against Naser Oric. You will receive all the assistance you require now to help you return back home at the earliest opportunity, and on behalf of everyone present here I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, and I wish you all the best in your work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, very quick matter that we need to be resolved because I need the courtroom reorganised for another sitting that I have which has three accused. So we need to do this very quickly. Next witness, number 46. You say five hours here and then you indicate 17th and 18th of May. What are your intentions? Because I don't see how we can finish this witness in two days if you are requiring five hours for yourself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that witness's testimony now will be scaled back quite a bit and we believe that that can be presented certainly by the Prosecution within a day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And the other day will be reserved for the Defence. Is would that be okay with you?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we stand adjourned until --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I do have one matter that refers to Judge Eser's question related to document, Prosecution Exhibit 54. I believe he --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You were right to point this because I too thought it was 54 at the beginning. We'll meet on Tuesday, and on Tuesday also please there will be a meeting in my Chamber between the first and the second session. And that will be housekeeping mostly. All right? But it will include also matters related to Rule 98 bis. Thank you. Have a nice weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 17th of May, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.
